scheme_name: Micro Finance Scheme for Self Help Groups (GTKVN)
description:
The Micro Finance Scheme for Self Help Groups (GTKVN) is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to empower women and promote financial inclusion. 

This scheme was introduced in 2001 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. 

The primary objective of the GTKVN scheme is to provide financial assistance to Self Help Groups (SHGs) to enable them to become self-sustainable. 

The scheme aims to enhance the income-generating capacity of women by providing them access to microfinance. 

The GTKVN scheme specifically targets women from economically weaker sections of society. 

It aims to promote entrepreneurship among women by providing them with the necessary financial support. 

The scheme has set a measurable target of forming and nurturing at least 1.5 million SHGs across the country by 2025. 

The financial assistance provided under the GTKVN scheme is aimed at facilitating various income-generating activities. 

Eligible SHGs can receive loans ranging from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000. 

The interest rate on these loans is generally around 7 to 10 percent per annum. 

The repayment period for these loans is typically between 1 to 3 years. 

The benefits of the GTKVN scheme extend beyond financial assistance. 

It also includes capacity building and skill development programs for women. 

These programs are designed to enhance the entrepreneurial skills of women in SHGs. 

The scheme also provides access to market linkages for the products produced by SHGs. 

This helps in improving the marketability of their goods and services. 

Eligibility criteria for the GTKVN scheme include being a member of a registered SHG. 

Members must also be women aged between 18 to 60 years. 

The annual income of the SHG members should not exceed ₹1,00,000. 

The application process for the GTKVN scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested women must form a Self Help Group. 

The SHG must be registered with the relevant government authority. 

Next, the SHG should prepare a project proposal outlining the intended use of the loan. 

This proposal must include details about the income-generating activity. 

The SHG must then submit the proposal to the nearest bank or financial institution. 

Required documents include the SHG registration certificate and identity proofs of the members. 

Once the proposal is submitted, the bank will assess the application. 

If approved, the loan amount will be disbursed to the SHG's bank account. 

The disbursement usually occurs within 15 to 30 days of approval. 

The GTKVN scheme also includes a provision for regular monitoring and evaluation. 

This ensures that the funds are utilized effectively for the intended purpose. 

The implementing authority for the GTKVN scheme is the Ministry of Rural Development. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this scheme. 

They are responsible for facilitating the formation of SHGs and providing necessary training. 

The scheme has seen significant success since its inception. 

As of 2023, over 10 million women have benefited from the GTKVN scheme. 

The scheme has contributed to a notable increase in the income levels of SHG members. 

Reports indicate that the average income of SHG members has increased by 30 percent since joining. 

The GTKVN scheme has also led to improved social status for women in rural areas. 

Women who have benefited from the scheme have reported increased decision-making power in their households. 

The scheme has also fostered a sense of community among women. 

They collaborate on various projects and support each other in their entrepreneurial endeavors. 

The GTKVN scheme is part of a broader strategy to promote women's empowerment in India. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of financial literacy among women. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted to educate women about financial management. 

These initiatives help women understand budgeting and savings. 

The GTKVN scheme has also been instrumental in promoting sustainable livelihoods. 

By supporting income-generating activities, it helps reduce poverty in rural areas. 

The scheme encourages women to engage in various sectors such as agriculture, handicrafts, and services. 

The government has allocated significant funds for the GTKVN scheme in recent budgets. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, ₹1,500 crores were earmarked for the scheme. 

This funding is aimed at expanding the reach of the scheme to more women. 

The GTKVN scheme also collaborates with various non-governmental organizations. 

These organizations assist in capacity building and providing technical support to SHGs. 

The success stories of SHG members have inspired many other women to join the movement. 

Women who have availed of the scheme have become role models in their communities. 

The GTKVN scheme continues to evolve based on feedback from beneficiaries. 

The government is committed to addressing challenges faced by SHGs. 

Regular assessments are conducted to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme's impact is monitored through various indicators such as income levels and employment rates. 

Overall, the Micro Finance Scheme for Self Help Groups (GTKVN) represents a vital step towards achieving gender equality and economic empowerment for women in India. 

It not only provides financial assistance but also fosters a supportive ecosystem for women entrepreneurs. 

The scheme has proven to be a powerful tool in transforming the lives of millions of women across the country. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a more inclusive and equitable society. 

The GTKVN scheme exemplifies the potential of microfinance as a catalyst for social change. 

It highlights the importance of empowering women as a means to drive economic growth. 

The ongoing success of the GTKVN scheme is a testament to the resilience and determination of women in India. 

As the scheme progresses, it is expected to reach even more women and create lasting change in rural communities.
